title: tud + Infinitive: A Wider Range of Skills

sections.title: The rule you already know
sections.content: Back in Unit 18 you learned that tud ("to be able to, to know how to") combines with an infinitive to state personal ability, and that it conjugates fully for every person: tudok, tudsz, tud, tudunk, tudtok, tudnak. That rule doesn't change here — this lesson just puts it to work with a bigger set of everyday skills, and with every person, not just "I".

sections.title: New skills with tud
rows: Károly can play the piano very well.

items.spanish: Zsófia ügyes: tud rajzolni, főzni és zongorázni is.
items.english: Zsófia is skilled: she can draw, cook, and play the piano too.
Can you (pl.) drive, or are you going by bus?

sections.content: is ("too, also") slots in right after the word it emphasizes, not at the end of the sentence like English "too" — tud rajzolni, főzni és zongorázni is puts is straight after zongorázni because that's the skill being added to the list.
